title: Preference Label Noise Injection: Characterizing RLHF Degradation Under Annotator Error

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Characterizing noise thresholds informs annotation quality standards. Useful but somewhat incremental — it confirms a known risk (noisy labels degrade RLHF) and quantifies the boundary.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training reward models on corrupted preference datasets and evaluating downstream policy quality. The full reward model training plus policy training pipeline is complex for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clean experimental design: one variable (noise level) with clear metric. But the full pipeline (corrupt data, train RM, train policy, evaluate) has multiple stages. Could be scoped to reward model quality only without policy training.
